x.Seismic Imaging Algorithm Depth: Covers advanced algorithms like RTM, FWI, and least-squares migration for accurate subsurface imaging. Strength shown by published benchmarks, proprietary methods, and successful complex reservoir imaging.
x.High-Performance Computing Scalability: Ability to run large-scale seismic processing on GPU/CPU clusters with efficient parallelization. Evidence includes petaflop-scale compute capacity, cloud integration, and processing turnaround times.
x.Multi-Client Data Library Breadth: Extent and quality of pre-processed seismic data packages licensed to multiple clients. Strength indicated by coverage of key basins, vintage, and number of active multi-client projects.

x.AI/ML Integration for Interpretation: Use of machine learning for automated fault picking, facies classification, and noise attenuation. Strength shown by validated AI models, patents, and adoption in commercial workflows.

y.Named Oil & Gas Customer Contracts: Publicly disclosed contracts with major oil & gas companies or national oil companies. Evidence includes contract values, duration, and client names in press releases or financial reports.
y.Global Processing Center Footprint: Number and location of seismic processing centers worldwide. Strength indicated by presence in key regions (e.g., Houston, London, Dubai, Singapore) and local technical staff.
y.Revenue & Backlog Growth: Financial performance metrics including annual revenue, growth rate, and contracted backlog. Evidence from public financial statements or investor presentations.
y.Strategic Partnerships & Alliances: Collaborations with technology providers, E&P companies, or research institutions. Evidence includes joint ventures, co-development agreements, and named partners.
y.Market Share in Seismic Processing: Estimated share of the global seismic data processing market. Strength shown by third-party market reports, competitive rankings, and client win rates.

The company structured its localized processing scale around a dedicated Gerencia de Procesamiento de Datos Geofísicos under its Exploration Services Division to oversee data workflows.
COMESA pursued technical scalability through equipment acquisition requests, such as seeking 587.7 million pesos for an autonomous nodal system for imaging the deep Ixachi field.

Project management workflows within COMESA incorporated machine learning and advanced data science to optimize workflows and enhance decision-making during the Ixachi 3D survey.

Compañía Mexicana de Exploraciones, S.A. de C.V. (COMESA) operates primarily as a subsidiary and longstanding contractor for Mexico's state oil company, Petróleos Mexicanos (PEMEX), which holds a 60% shareholding in COMESA as documented by Mexico Business News.
COMESA has historically provided land seismic surveys, engineering projects, consulting, and well services directly to PEMEX as reported by Mexico Business News.

The company faced severe financial difficulties exacerbated by the cancellation of the Ixachi project with PEMEX, initiating bankruptcy and subsequent liquidation proceedings approved by SENER as detailed by Mexico Business News.

COMESA is headquartered in Mexico City, Mexico, focusing its operational and geophysical activities predominantly on onshore, transition, and offshore zones within Mexico as outlined in the PEMEX Corporate Document.

Its strategic footprint centers around domestic seismic data processing and interpretation services for Mexican basins rather than maintaining a multi-continental or global processing center network as noted by BNamericas.

COMESA suffered severe financial deterioration and significant operational losses, leading to an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders on April 17, 2023, which approved the dissolution and liquidation of the company as reported by Mexico Business News.

The company initiated legal proceedings to declare bankruptcy driven by non-payment issues and the cancellation of major projects like Ixachi, reflecting negative revenue growth and a depleted backlog as outlined by Mexico Business News.

COMESA was structured as a joint venture-style corporate entity involving the Mexican government/PEMEX and private interests to deliver exploration and geological mapping solutions as described by BNamericas.

Its primary institutional alliance has been its captive subsidiary relationship with state-owned Petróleos Mexicanos (PEMEX), rather than active commercial technology alliances with independent global seismic multi-client firms, as documented by Mexico Business News.
COMESA held a niche domestic market position handling land seismic surveys and data processing tied heavily to PEMEX's domestic exploration agenda in Mexico as stated by BNamericas.

With SENER approving the formal dissolution, liquidation, and appointment of the Institute to Return Stolen Goods to the People as liquidator, the company's active market share has effectively receded to zero as documented by Mexico Business News.
